newsitem.title: BOLIVIA: SOCCER-PASSARELLA REITERATES COPA PULL-OUT THREAT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PASSARELLA REITERATES COPA PULL-OUT THREAT.

text.p: Argentina coach Daniel Passarella on Wednesday reiterated his threat to pull his team out of the Copa America if they were forced to play their quarter-final at high altitiude in La Paz.
Passarella, who got full backing from his players, was furious at a rule-change made on Tuesday that could alter the venue of his team's quarter-final.
"I'm not going to La Paz. I don't care about the consequences when I belive I am right, when I defend my ideas, my principles and my convictions," he said.
"I've cooled down a bit since last night but the fact that I've cooled down hasn't changed my way of thinking and I want to publicly thank the players for their solidarity," he said.

Argentina drew 1-1 with Paraguay on Tuesday to finish second in group A and earn a quarter-final tie against the team that finishes second in group B, which features Bolivia, Peru, Venezuela and Uruguay.
The match had been scheduled for Sucre, which at 2,700 metres above sea level is only 100 metres higher than Argentina's first round venue Cochabamba.
But on Tuesday, the Copa America organisers announced that if hosts Bolivia finish second in group B, the game will be held in La Paz at 3,600 metres above sea level.

"The simple truth is that you cannot change the rules in the middle of the tournament," said Passarella, who found out about the alteration when a reporter asked him his opinion about it during a media conference after Tuesday's game.
He got full support from his players. "Our position is the same as Daniel's," said midfielder Marcelo Gallardo. "Daniel has our unanimous backing, the rules must be stuck too," he said.
"These are not excuses, it's not the same playing here as it is at sea level or in La Paz," said Christian Bassedas.

Passarella, who has brought a second-string team to the Copa, is already angry at the timing of the competition, which is crammed between the region's World Cup qualifying matches. He also claims the World Cup qualifying competition itself is too long.

He has sore memories of Argentina's last trip to La Paz when they were beaten 2-1 by Bolivia in a World Cup qualifier in April. Argentina had two players sent off and were involved in a brawl that held up play for 10 minutes.
Argentines are also angry that they were placed in Cochabamba, while arch-rivals Brazil have been placed in Santa Cruz, the only sea-level venue.
The final of the competition will only be in La Paz if Bolivia reach it. Otherwise, it will be held in Santa Cruz.
Brazil coach Mario Zagallo said he was not worried about going to La Paz. "I want to play in La Paz, because that will mean we have reached the final," he said.
"I prefer to play at sea level but if you come to this competition, you have to be prepared to play at altitude otherwise Bolivia would not be able to host it."
A source for the South American Football Confederation (CSF) said Argentina could face sanctions if they carried out their threat.
Group B was due to be settled later on Wednesday with Bolivia needing a point from their last game against Uruguay to ensure first place and avert the crisis.
